summary: The 2D screening label is not_2d_applicable, and Studio did not run (simulation status: skipped; simulation_allowed false). The selected scenario is Figure 6(a)/(b) of W3006943355: transient maximum temperature, 200-450 ms, for the mem2 and com2 workload sets under Baseline DVFS, FLC and FBTM. It comes from a 3D-stacked system with 4 cores, 3 TSV-connected L2 cache layers, closed-loop fuzzy DVFS and dynamic cache bank gating, simulated with HotSpot, gem5 and McPAT. The extracted experiment is a custom_2d_steady with an empty floorplan and no power_w, so the input gate failed (a custom experiment needs 1-128 blocks and a power_w object). The scientific gate also failed. Many evidence items lack a valid page or pinned asset locator, no cited steady/transient regime or paper thermal observable was recorded, the adversarial checks are unresolved, and independent review is pending. No Studio temperature exists, so comparison_valid is false and no numerical comparison is made. A custom 2D steady run would have no transient trace in any case. The paper's only quantitative statements are approximate and text-based: about 3 degC average reduction for FLC/FBTM versus baseline, fluctuation within 0.5 degC versus up to 3.5 degC for the baseline, and a plotted axis of roughly 75-81 degC. These are not per-scenario scalars and cannot be matched to any 2D steady quantity. Qualitatively, the paper suggests that active temperature control and cache gating can reduce peak temperature and its variation in 3D stacks, but this run neither confirms nor refutes that claim. The result is a screening outcome only, not a replication.
limitations: Studio did not run, so there is no simulated result to compare against the paper.
The extracted experiment has no floorplan blocks and no per-block power; geometry and watts are not published, and total chip power must not be split without a published rule.
The paper scenario is a 3D stack (1 core layer plus 3 cache layers, TSVs, vertical super-core model) that a single-layer 2D steady model cannot represent.
The observable is a transient, controller-in-the-loop maximum temperature trace with a runtime-varying threshold, whereas a custom 2D steady run yields no transient trace.
Solver and toolchain mismatch: the paper uses HotSpot grid mode with gem5/McPAT power traces and a compact super-core model, with no published configuration.
Ambient temperature, Vdd, frequency levels, thermal resistances (Ramb, Rv), heat sink, TIM, layer thicknesses and package are all unspecified.

No numeric curve values are published for Figure 6; only approximate text statements (about 3 degC average reduction, 0.5 vs 3.5 degC fluctuation). Digitizing the curves would add substantial uncertainty, and the 3 degC figure is an average across experiments, not a value for this scenario.
No paper-linked assets, code, configs or data were found (checked_no_links), and the com2 workload lists only three applications while the text describes four.
Feasibility gate failures include missing page/asset locators on the evidence items, no cited thermal observable or regime, unresolved adversarial checks and pending independent review.
Because the gate controls the verdict, the final verdict is not_2d_applicable with comparison_valid false; no exact replication or numerical agreement is claimed.
